findings.rationale: The workstation fs_stat snapshot for /tmp/.font-unix/cache-0a91.bin (16,679,959 bytes, owner kcole) shows a 2026-10-11 12:23:25 time in one field and a 2026-11-10 12:25:35 time in another. That is a metadata discrepancy in a 16.7 MB file that sits near the 12:24 outbound transfer. The snapshot is host-local and not forwarded, so it does not show who changed it.
verifier_notes: the time window is wider than 30 minutes; too broad to verify

findings.rationale: Tap flow from 10.20.1.21 to 10.20.9.67:8080 sent 16,683,146 bytes out over about 11 seconds. This is above the 5 MB bulk threshold and the destination is not an approved bulk destination. The source is the same address as the adm-bsato session 315 at 12:26:48. Source-host mapping for 10.20.1.21 is not confirmed in the bundle, so host is set to records on the basis of that session.
verifier_notes: no cited record is a bulk transfer observed at the tap from this host, or the command that launched one

findings.rationale: The adm-bsato session 315 on records came from 10.20.1.21. The brief's admin_sources are only 10.20.1.90 (adm-lt-01) and 10.20.0.250 (vpn-gw-01), so this is an unapproved source address. The session ran the log-forwarder stop. Session 314 came from the approved 10.20.1.90.
verifier_notes: a session on this host was opened from another monitored host outside the stated access policy

findings.rationale: adm-bsato ran 'sudo systemctl stop log-forwarder' on records at 12:27:34 (session 315). Collector copies show the stop and the later restart at 12:29:46. Collector copies of records' access.log jump from seq 501 (12:27:21) to seq 502 (12:30:32), so records-app lines in the gap were not forwarded.
alternative_explanations: Planned maintenance by an admin; no approved change record in the brief covers it.
verifier_notes: a recorded stop command opens this collection gap and no approved change record covers it

In that session it stopped log-forwarder and the forwarder was restarted about two minutes later. A 16.7 MB outbound flow from 10.20.1.21 to 10.20.9.67:8080 occurred minutes earlier. The human operator is not established. Account use does not identify a person.

summary: Bundle bndl-e34df55aa1a3df3e, Northside Clinic. The main supported finding is a window of about 12:24 to 12:30 UTC on 2026-11-10. Account adm-bsato opened records session 315 from 10.20.1.21, which is not an approved admin source. The session stopped log-forwarder at 12:27:34 (collector copies match) and the forwarder restarted at 12:29:46. Collector copies of records' access.log show a gap in that window. At 12:24:54 a 16.7 MB outbound flow from 10.20.1.21 went to 10.20.9.67:8080, which is not an approved bulk destination. Separately, a workstation file in /tmp/.font-unix has inconsistent timestamps. Approved transfers (aokafor's small lab uploads to 10.20.8.20, and a 16.7 MB backup to stor-nas-01) are noted as policy-consistent. Attribution: the account used is adm-bsato; the human operator is not established.
open_questions: Which host is 10.20.1.21, and what is 10.20.9.67? The flow record's source host is not mapped in the bundle.

What was the content of the 16.7 MB flow at 12:24:54, and does it match the staged file /tmp/.font-unix/cache-0a91.bin? The file's timestamps are inconsistent, but nothing in the bundle links it to the flow.
Why did the records adm-bsato shell history stop at 8 lines and not show the 10.20.1.21 session's commands? The shell history for that session is not in the bundle.
The sensor and reference comparison was not performed in this pass; no temperature finding is made.
Records access.log is host-local, and the rotated segment is archived off-host. The gap in collector copies may not match the host's own log.
